You know the NSA is listening, watching, and reading everything you do online. You know every email, text, and IM you send is being recorded and tagged. You know that governments violate your privacy at every turn. There's a very simple solution in using strong encryption. PGP/GnuPG for emails. OTR for IM. TOR for web browsing.

But in my entire address book I have a grand total of 4 people who use encryption for communication.

So what's stopping you? What would make it better?

EDIT Links:

GnuPG - Gnu Privacy Guard https://www.gnupg.org/

EnigMail - GnuPG Plugin for Thunderbird - https://www.enigmail.net

OTR for pidgin - Off The Record IM encryption - https://otr.cypherpunks.ca/

TOR - The Onion Router, encrypts and bounces traffic around to provide anonymity and access to .onion sites - https://www.torproject.org/

TOX.im - secure encrypted chat, video chat, and file transfer - https://tox.im

Google End-to-End Encryption for gmail - http://googleonlinesecurity.blogspot.com/2014/06/making-end-to-end-encryption-easier-to.html
Why don't you use encryption? What would change your mind?
I guess most people aren't tech-savvy/don't care enough to use it for general things.
I can understand not being tech-savvy enough, but people care enough to yell about the NSA all day long but not enough to download an app to protect themselves?

I'll tell you exactly what's stopping me: large percentages of people with apathy and unwillingness to learn about any of it. I use my email, text and all that about 95% for personal use, and only a slim margin of it going towards actual, work-related, important stuff. So of this big ol' pool of people that I correspond with on a daily basis, most of them simply don't see a need to use it. A large subsection of that swath doesn't even know what 'encryption' means, and a slightly smaller subsection of that wouldn't even know how to implement it without me either doing it for them, or walking them through it step by step and fixing every issue along the way.

I honestly think that the only way privacy-based encryption is going to take off is by some major outlet, or two, or all of them, making it a default-able feature. Sad as that may be, I simply don't see the public, on the whole, taking the time to learn about the importance and the need for using it, let alone diving in to actually learning how to implement it.

Most people just don't care.
